stories.title: Self-hosted account registration, login and lifecycle
stories.journey: Users create or sign into one account on the owned service, manage profile/security and recover or delete the account without making local/offline use dependent on it.
tests: Standards-based OIDC/PKCE or audited identity service completes registration, verification and login in a deployed fixture.
MFA/recovery and credential changes invalidate affected sessions without account enumeration.
Refresh rotation, logout and session management reject stolen/reused expired tokens.
Account deletion/recovery revokes devices and follows explicit retention/export policy.
Local opencode2 remains usable without network or hosted account and never silently uploads history.

stories.title: Explicit PC enrollment and single-use pairing
stories.journey: From opencode2 pair/connect, enroll a device key and confirm a short-lived account-bound QR/code with visible identity/fingerprint and permissions.
tests: User signs in, confirms the PC identity and pairs exactly the intended account/device.
Expired, reused, brute-forced or another-account pairing codes fail without enrollment.
QR/deep links contain only single-use challenge material, never provider keys or long-lived credentials.
Concurrent redemption creates one enrollment and produces a clear already-used result.
Cancel/unpair clears pending authority and requires explicit consent before re-enrollment.

stories.title: Versioned remote control protocol and scoped authorization
stories.journey: Authenticate every remote command/subscription and authorize account, device, workspace, session, operation, expiry and policy version before routing.
tests: Valid scoped commands route to the intended connected PC/session.
Cross-account/device/workspace/session identifiers cannot access or mutate another scope.
Unsupported protocol versions and oversized/malformed frames fail closed with typed errors.
Command IDs, sequence/cursor fields and operation digests have explicit retry/replay semantics.
Revoked or stale capability epochs reject existing sockets and queued commands before execution.

stories.title: Named Cloudflare Tunnel gateway deployment
stories.journey: Deploy the owned account/control gateway behind a named Cloudflare Tunnel; expose only authenticated application routes, not the PC daemon directly.
tests: A real authorized staging named tunnel reaches the authenticated gateway over TLS.
Unauthenticated internet requests cannot reach agent, admin, metrics or internal origin routes.
HTTP/WebSocket upgrade and required event streaming work through the selected deployed transport.
Ingress has a deny catch-all and origin binding/firewall prevents bypass.
Tunnel credentials rotate without leaking to clients or logs; quick-tunnel/demo behavior is not production evidence.

stories.title: PC outbound connector and connection ownership
stories.journey: An opted-in PC maintains an authenticated outbound connection to the gateway and exposes only granted application capabilities without inbound port forwarding.
tests: A paired PC behind NAT receives and responds to an authorized control request.
Certificate/hostname/token validation rejects forged gateways and mismatched device credentials.
Sleep/resume/network loss uses bounded jittered reconnect and truthful offline status.
Disabling remote mode cancels and joins the connector with no residual listeners or credentials in logs.
Backpressure, heartbeat timeout and message size caps protect local execution and memory.

stories.title: Device inventory, presence and account dashboard
stories.journey: The same account lists paired PCs, their capabilities/status and explicit rename/disconnect/revoke actions.
tests: Two PCs appear under one account with distinct immutable device IDs.
Heartbeat expiry and PC sleep show offline/last-seen rather than false live availability.
Another account cannot discover device names, metadata or existence through API errors.
Rename/disconnect is reflected on connected clients with audit records.
Pagination and per-account device quotas remain bounded under repeated enrollment.

stories.title: Remote multi-workspace, multi-session and tab routing
stories.journey: Clients open multiple independent tabs across PCs/workspaces/sessions while all execution stays on the correct daemon.
tests: Two phones and a local TUI control different sessions without cross-routing prompts.
Tab state/drafts are client-local while session history and running work are daemon-owned.
Concurrent rename/archive/fork operations converge through versioned events.
Closing a mobile tab does not kill a background session unless explicitly requested.
Membership revocation removes subscriptions and blocks subsequent queued actions.

stories.title: Remote prompt, model, agent and interruption controls
stories.journey: A phone starts/steers/stops real PC coding turns, chooses allowed model/effort/agent and observes the same transcript as the local terminal.
tests: Phone-origin prompt invokes the same engine and real fixture tool as a local prompt.
Model/effort/subagent selections persist and affect actual requests.
Interrupt reaches the intended running turn and preserves recoverable history.
A duplicate submission ID does not create a second turn; ambiguous effects are not blindly retried.
Unauthorized or offline devices produce clear errors rather than queued invisible execution.

stories.title: Remote approval review with explicit human authority
stories.journey: Trusted paired users inspect exact tool/diff/scope details on a phone and approve/deny within explicit remote policy, never treating account login as unrestricted authority.
tests: A valid approval matches operation digest, device, workspace, requester and expiration.
Two clients racing approve/deny yield one deterministic decision and execution.
Replay or changed operation content invalidates an approval without side effects.
Local-only/human-only restrictions and protected resources remain enforced from remote clients.
Revocation/phone logout/PC policy change invalidates pending authority and records the outcome.

stories.title: Authorized remote file, diff and artifact workflows
stories.journey: Review authorized workspace files/diffs/artifacts on the phone and apply explicitly approved changes through existing safe services.
tests: Allowed file/diff/artifact views match PC state and preserve version/conflict information.
Traversal, symlink escape, secret paths and unauthorized workspace IDs are denied without content leakage.
Concurrent edits require version preconditions and never overwrite unrelated changes.
Uploads/downloads enforce content, size, quota and cancellation cleanup.
Artifact apply/run uses the same approval/sandbox path rather than a separate remote bypass.

stories.title: Constrained remote PTY session control
stories.journey: Explicitly authorized users operate a bounded project-scoped terminal session with resize, input, output and termination; this is not unrestricted desktop/RDP access.
tests: Granted PTY input/output and resize work through the real gateway to a fixture workspace process.
Read-only or ungranted clients cannot inject terminal input or start a shell.
Environment, filesystem, network and human-only restrictions apply to subprocesses.
Disconnect/reconnect follows a documented lease/retention policy without orphaned processes.
Flooded output/input and hostile terminal sequences respect byte/rate/scrollback budgets.

stories.title: Replay, offline state and conflict-safe reconnection
stories.journey: Recover live sessions after mobile backgrounding, tunnel restart and PC reconnection with cursors/snapshots and explicit pending-command outcomes.
tests: Reconnect from a valid cursor rebuilds the same session without duplicate messages.
Expired cursors trigger bounded resync and clearly invalidate stale UI state.
Commands sent around disconnect report committed, rejected or uncertain outcomes; no claimed universal exactly-once effects.
Concurrent edits and control actions use conflict/version checks.
Offline drafts are preserved locally but sensitive side effects never auto-replay after authority expiry.

stories.title: Device/token revocation and credential lifecycle
stories.journey: Revoke a lost phone or PC, rotate credentials and terminate active capabilities and streams without disrupting unrelated paired devices.
tests: Revocation closes active subscriptions/control streams and rejects new commands.
Queued operations are reauthorized at execution time after credential epoch changes.
Refresh-token reuse and cloned/expired device credentials are rejected.
Re-enrollment requires fresh pairing, not reuse of a revoked challenge.
Audit and UI show revocation propagation and the documented maximum enforcement delay.

stories.title: Remote gateway adversarial security
stories.journey: Prove gateway and PC authorization remain effective against hostile internet clients and compromised unprivileged sessions.
tests: Cross-tenant IDOR and websocket subscription/action escalation fail without side effects.
CSRF, Origin/CORS, DNS rebinding and forged forwarding headers cannot bypass authority.
Gateway destinations cannot be used for SSRF or arbitrary reverse proxying.
Login/pairing/command/upload floods encounter bounded rate/byte/account limits and redacted audit logs.
Stored/rendered hostile content, token leakage, reconnect replay and local-origin bypass are tested end to end.

stories.title: Self-hosted operations, backup and quotas
stories.journey: An operator can deploy, upgrade, back up, restore and observe the owned service with explicit capacity/security controls and no per-user manual tunnel setup.
tests: Documented staging deployment initializes account storage and gateway without exposing administrative defaults.
Backup/restore preserves identity/device/session metadata and treats encryption keys separately.
Upgrade/rollback handles schema/protocol compatibility with old supported PC and phone clients.
Per-account/device/session quotas and retention have visible errors rather than silent user-history deletion.
Health/metrics/logging detect disconnect, lag and auth failures without containing secrets or full transcripts.

stories.title: Installed iOS app, account login and secure session
stories.journey: Install a real iOS client, select the owned service, sign in through the system auth flow and view authorized PCs using Keychain-protected credentials.
tests: Signed development/test build installs on a real iOS device and completes account login.
PKCE/state/deep-link validation rejects intercepted or mismatched auth callbacks.
Tokens use Keychain and are absent from insecure logs, screenshots and plain preference storage.
Logout/expiry/revocation returns to a safe signed-out UI and closes subscriptions.
VoiceOver, dynamic text, safe areas and keyboard navigation work on login and device list.

stories.title: Installed Android app, account login and secure session
stories.journey: Install a real Android client, choose the owned service and sign into the same account with Keystore-backed secure credentials and validated app links.
tests: Signed test build installs on a real Android device and completes login against the deployed gateway.
PKCE/state/app-link validation rejects interception and mismatched callbacks.
Sensitive credentials are protected with Keystore-backed storage and excluded from backups/logs.
Logout, refresh rotation and revocation close active authority and clear sensitive UI state.
TalkBack, font scaling, keyboard and navigation controls work on login and device list.

stories.title: Mobile multi-PC workspace/session tabs
stories.journey: On both platforms browse PCs/projects, open/reorder/close tabs and navigate parent/child sessions with independent drafts and truthful online state.
tests: Two PCs and several sessions stay distinctly routed across independent tabs.
Restart restores selected tabs/drafts while daemon state is revalidated.
Rename/archive/fork/subagent changes from the local TUI appear correctly on phones.
Small screens, rotation, keyboard and accessibility labels remain usable.
Long lists/history are virtualized; offline/empty/error/loading states have explicit recovery actions.

stories.title: Mobile prompt, tools, approvals, diff and PTY interaction
stories.journey: Users compose prompts, switch models/agents, view streamed code/tool output, approve scoped operations and use granted file/diff/PTY controls on both platforms.
tests: Phone prompt edits a real PC fixture file through the normal approved coding turn.
Touch/keyboard interruption cancels the intended turn and updates the local TUI.
Approval UI shows exact operation/scope and cannot approve stale or modified actions.
Code/diff/artifact/terminal views support scroll/copy/resize without executing hostile display sequences.
Platform permission, offline and authorization failures preserve drafts and expose accurate recovery actions.

stories.title: Mobile background/reconnect, notifications and privacy
stories.journey: Switch networks, background/kill/reopen the app and safely resume; optional notifications disclose no code or secrets and never assume continuous mobile background execution.
tests: Background/foreground and process recreation recover cursor/snapshot and pending draft state.
Wi-Fi/cellular transitions and gateway restart do not duplicate prompts or side effects.
APNs/FCM notification opt-in and deep-link routing revalidate account/device/session authority.
Lockscreen notification contents omit code, secrets and detailed approval payloads by default.
Revocation while backgrounded prevents reconnect; battery/network usage remains within measured targets.

stories.title: Real-phone full remote journey acceptance
stories.journey: On real iOS and Android devices, use one account to pair PCs, control concurrent sessions, approve a tool, reconnect and revoke through the deployed named tunnel.
tests: Record install/login/pair/control journeys on at least one real device per platform.
Run two PCs, two phones and local TUI concurrently without tenant/session cross-talk.
Tunnel restart, PC sleep and phone backgrounding preserve truthful recoverable state.
Lost-device revocation prevents active and queued control on the real deployment.
Evidence includes exact mobile builds, PC/gateway revision, tunnel configuration and actual tests; browser mocks do not count.
